newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma to vote on spending cuts on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma to vote on spending cuts on Monday.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament decided on Friday to postpone to Monday a vote on amendments to the 1997 budget which the government says are crucial to sort out the country's chaotic finances.

A special commission set up to try to overcome differences between parliament and the government failed to reach a compromise on Thursday and parliament was due to discuss and vote on its own proposals on Friday.
But Alexander Zhukov, deputy head of the State Duma's budget committee, told parliament: "The vote on spending cuts is put on Monday's agenda at 12.30 (0830 GMT)."
Ministers originally wanted to slash spending by a fifth, or by 108 trillion roubles ($18.7 billion), because of a shortfall in tax revenues.
But parliament, afraid its long-suffering electorate will suffer from the spending squeeze, is insisting on much smaller cuts.

Its first proposal is a plan to cut revenues by 42 trillion roubles instead of the 88 trillion which the government agreed to. The second would let parliament off the hook by giving the government sole responsibility for the fate of the 1997 budget.
Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Yakov Urinson told Interfax news agency on Thursday the government would not agree to a spending cut, or sequestration, smaller than 80 trillion roubles.
"Further cuts to sequestration plans will become a catastrophe," he said, adding the ideal size of the spending cut was 120 trillion roubles.
The spending cuts are just one of a series of bills which the cabinet is trying to force through parliament in the hope of dragging Russia from its deep post-communist recession.
Ministers scored a victory on Thursday when the chamber gave its initial approval to a tax code which the International Monetary Fund sees as a key to further reform.
